sections.heading: Observation, spacing, parking and passing restrictions
sections.markdown:
# Observation, spacing, parking and passing restrictions

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Look well ahead rather than focusing only on the area immediately in front of the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
The guide recommends a visual lead of twenty to thirty seconds along the intended travel path. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
If a curve, hill or vehicle blocks the view ahead, reduce speed and prepare to adjust the travel path. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Watch for vehicles entering the roadway, moving into the lane or turning ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Brake lights ahead give advance warning that other traffic is slowing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
A green signal that has been showing for a long time may change before the vehicle reaches it; prepare for a stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Early, gradual changes give drivers behind more time to respond. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
To measure the visual lead, time travel from the current position to a fixed object ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
The guide estimates that reacting and stopping at sixty miles per hour can require about four to five seconds or 359 feet under good conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
The guide estimates about two to three seconds or 123 feet for reacting and stopping at thirty miles per hour under good conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
Visibility must provide enough distance to stop before an obstacle in the travel path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
An intersection includes a place where traffic streams cross or merge, including driveways and parking-lot entrances. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Approaching a junction, check cross traffic, approaching vehicles, pedestrians, controls, visibility and the road surface. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
After stopping at an intersection, look left, then right, then left again before proceeding. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
Continue checking for crossing traffic even when other drivers face a stop sign or red light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Enter an intersection only with a clear path through it so a later stop will not block the crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Busy sidewalks, playgrounds, school grounds and parking areas call for extra side-to-side scanning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A03
A left-turning driver must yield to approaching vehicles traveling straight or turning right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A03
Before completing a left turn, make sure vehicles or pedestrians will not trap the turning vehicle in opposing traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A03
Before a right turn, check traffic approaching from the left, opposing left-turners and crossing pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A03
Slow on a railroad approach and check both track directions for trains or maintenance equipment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A03
Check rear traffic before changing lanes, slowing, entering from the roadside or descending a long hill. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
Before a lane change, check mirrors for vehicles in the destination lane or about to pass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
A blind spot is an area around the vehicle that the mirrors do not show. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
Check the blind spot by looking over the shoulder toward the intended lane change. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
Do not look away from the forward path for too long while checking behind or beside the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A03
The guide recommends identifying a four-to-five-second traffic gap before a lane change. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A03
Signal, check the intended lane again, adjust speed, enter it safely and cancel the signal after changing lanes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A03
Check mirrors while slowing, particularly at an unexpected turn into a driveway or parking space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A03
On a long downhill grade, watch behind for large vehicles approaching rapidly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A04
Adjust the interior rear-view mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A04
The guide describes positioning side-mirror views to overlap the interior mirror’s rearward view. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A04
Perception distance is the distance traveled between seeing a hazard and recognizing it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A04
Reaction distance is the distance traveled after recognizing danger and before physically applying the brakes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A04
Braking distance is the travel that occurs while the brakes are being applied. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A04
Total stopping distance includes perception, reaction and braking distances [A04] [A05].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A05
Actual stopping needs vary with response time, road and weather conditions, vehicle weight, brakes and tires. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A05
Higher speed increases braking distance and the potential severity of a crash. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A05
The guide’s three-second following check starts when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed roadside object. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A05
If the following vehicle reaches that object before three seconds have elapsed, the gap is too short under the guide’s basic rule. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A05
Increase the gap and repeat the timing check until the basic following interval is met. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]
